messages:
Evan L: Quick check — can we lock the weekly triage call cadence for Q2? Our backlog is drifting and we need a lightweight owner rotation.
Sana R: +1. I'm fine keeping Wed 10am but would prefer 30m max.
Mike T: Wed 10 works for me but 30m feels tight when we have infra bugs. Can we do 40m?
Jess C: I vote for 30m for steady state, with an opt-in extended slot (extra 15m) if the queue is bad.
Anita P: Proposal: 30m fixed cadence, owners rotate weekly (round-robin across eng leads), and last 5m for owner assignments + follow-ups.
Evan L: That sounds good. Rotation order suggestion: infra -> runtime -> platform -> product -> eng-sre. Whoever's owner brings up top 3 items beforehand.
Sana R: Can we add a short agenda template the owner pastes into the channel before the call? e.g.,
```
Agenda (30m):
1) Top 3 blockers from bug queue (5m)
2) Backlog triage / owner assignment (10m)
3) Quick rollouts / incidents (5m)
4) Follow-ups & action items (10m)
```
Mike T: Looks good. Suggest making item 2 explicit: "Assign owners + ETA" so things don't linger.
Jess C: I'll own next week's call (infra week) and will paste the agenda in #eng by EOD Monday. @Evan L can you add the rotation list to the calendar invite?
Evan L: Yep, I'll update the recurring invite and add calendar notes with rotation order and the agenda template.
deploy-bot: Reminder: recurring meeting updated by Evan L.
Anita P: One more tweak — can we surface any high-priority regressions in the thread using the tag :rotating_light: to force the extended slot? Owner can call it at the start.
Sana R: Good idea. We'll use :rotating_light: in the agenda post.
Mike T: OK, final call: Wed 10am, 30m fixed + optional 15m extension if flagged, weekly round-robin owners. Everyone good?
Jess C: good from me :+1:
Evan L: Good. I'll update invite, rotation, and add the short checklist for owners.
Sana R: Thanks — will ping owners mid-week if they forget.
Anita P: I'll create a tiny template doc to track owners & past action items. Link in #eng once ready.
Evan L: Closing thread — thanks all.
